relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther
relations.role: Professor and Head of the Department of Far Eastern Studies
relations.evidence: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther (17 March 1917 – 11 March 2006) was a German Buddhist philosopher and Professor and Head of the Department of Far Eastern Studies at the University of Saskatchewan

relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther
relations.evidence: Günther went to Munich for further study after graduation, earning the Ph.D. degree in 1939.

relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther
relations.evidence: Four years later he received the degree Dr. Phil. Habil. in Vienna.

relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther
relations.evidence: Amongst the most influential of his European mentors were Professor Wilhelm Geiger, a specialist in Pali and Sinhalese, and Walter Wüst – both of Munich.

relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther
relations.evidence: He progressed to teaching and taught at Vienna University from 1943 to 1950.

relations.subject: Erich Frauwallner
relations.evidence: Guenther left in 1950, refusing to serve under the rehabilitated ex-Nazi, Erich Frauwallner, whose academic chair had been restored to him.

relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther

relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther

relations.subject: Herbert Vighnāntaka Günther
relations.role: Head of the Department of Comparative Philosophy and Buddhist Studies
relations.evidence: He then went to the Sanskrit University in Varanasi, where he was Head of the Department of Comparative Philosophy and Buddhist Studies from 1958 to 1963.
